Coaching from a phone · re-evaluation
The arc
    Coaches Portal · the phone · a re-evaluation

    Coaching from a phone, end to end

    A head coach on a Premium team opens the portal the way most of them will: on the bus, at the fence, in the car park after practice, one thumb. This is every screen they reach in a game week and a practice week, read as built on 19 September 2026 at 390 pixels wide — what each one shows, how it feels in one hand, and where I would change its shape. The walk is the record; the tabs above hold one proposal per stage, added as each stage is ruled.

    How to read this

    • Eleven stations, in the order a coach meets them on a phone. Each one: what is on the screen as built (with the capture and its measurements), my assessment (what works, what gets in the way, what I’d change), and one to three shape questions with Keep · Reshape · Not yet. A notes box under each, and a paste-back summary at the end.
    • Then Standing back: seven rules that cut across every station — the bar and its roads, the screen budget, today-first, one figure and one qualifier, the field floor, where “Saved” lives, tables on a phone. Rule those and most station questions fall out.
    • The 0 · The shell tab is the first stage drawn as before/after at true size — open this page on your phone for that tab; the frames are 390px wide and do not reflow. Later stages get their own tab once the one before is ruled.

    Where I walked

    • 34 screens captured at 390×844 (the iPhone 14/15 class) and six again at 360×780 (the common Android), signed in as the head coach with every grant. No sideways scroll anywhere at either width.
    • Every screen was measured, not just looked at: page height in screens, words on the first screen, controls under the 44px tap floor, words set at the two smallest type steps (11px and 10px), and the chrome pinned to the viewport.
    • Interactions were driven: the More sheet to its bottom, the Schedule’s three views and the event sheet, a chat room and its composer, the live plan, the lineup grid swiped, the console scrolled, a roster row tapped on its blank side.
    • Practices and Skills & Goals were re-evaluated this month; I read them here only as phone screens and do not reopen those rulings.

    The screen budget — what a coach gets of 844 pixels

    Before any content, every team screen pins a two-line team masthead (59px, collapsing to 36 once you scroll) and the bottom bar (72px), and most draw a page-title row (about 64px). Four screens, to scale; the numbers are measured on the fixture.

    Hatched = pinned to the viewport on every team screen (131px at rest, 108 once scrolled). Tinted = a row the screen draws before its own content. Measured with the browser’s own geometry, not read off a picture. The console is the exception worth naming: its pinned card and action bar are the screen’s content, and it is the best phone screen in the portal — station 5.
    0

    The shell — the bar, the More sheet, and what is pinned

    Before any task: can a coach holding the phone tell where they are, reach the tool they came for, and keep most of the screen for the work?

    Every team screen …/coaches/teams/{id}/… · the bottom bar · More · the pinned masthead · the page-title row
    On the screen, as built

    The bar: Overview · Schedule · Chat · Roster · More (the four primaries owner-picked 29 June; Chat and More carry unread badges; the bar hides itself under any sheet). More opens a 210px-wide popover anchored to the tab, 591px tall, holding sixteen rows over 1,055px — so eight are visible and the rest are reached by scrolling inside it: Notifications · Your teams (2) · Season (Practice plans · Lineups · Tournaments) · Progress (Skills & Goals · Insights) · Money · Communication (Email families) · Team (Tryouts · Staff · Documents · Settings) · Help · Sign out. Money, Communication, Team, Help and Sign out are under its fold.

    The masthead: team name over “club · 2026 Season · 3-2-1” with the “?” at the right, 59px, pinned; it collapses to a 36px one-liner once the page scrolls. The page-title row below it: icon tile · title · the phone symbol (a lime “+” on Schedule and Roster, a “+ ▾” menu on Schedule) — about 64px, not pinned. On Overview the row’s right-hand control is a bare progress ring with no number or word (the team-setup chip, ring-only on a phone).

    pinned at rest 131px · scrolled 108pxMore popover 210 × 591 of 390 × 844rows in More 16 · visible 8taps to Practice plans 2 + a scroll

    How it feels to use — my assessment

    What works

    • Four tabs and More is the right count. A thumb reaches all five; the labels are plain words; the active tab is unmistakable. The bar gets out of the way under sheets, and it wears the warm skin.
    • What is waiting bubbles up. Unread chat on Chat, unread notifications on More — a coach never opens the sheet to find out.
    • The masthead collapses. On scroll the two lines become one 36px line; that is the right phone behaviour and it was measured working on every screen.
    • The page-title row already follows the phone rule on Schedule, Roster and Lineups: title · symbol · “?”. The create is a lime “+”, the export a glyph.

    What gets in the way

    • The three tools you named as phone-first — Practice plans, Lineups, Skills & Goals — are two taps and a scroll away, inside a 210px popover. It is a desktop dropdown drawn at the bottom of a phone: half its width is the page showing through, half its rows are under its own fold, and a coach who lands on Season has no cue that Team, Help and Sign out exist below. The sheet does not collapse its groups (right — a sheet is opened to find something), but it does not fit either.
    • The masthead repeats the team’s name on every screen at rest, 59px, over a page that names itself 20px below. A single-team coach reads their own team name on every open. Its two-line form exists for the desktop’s identity hierarchy; a phone needs the one-line form from the start on every screen that has a title of its own — and the chat room, where it stacks on a second header, shows the cost most (station 3).
    • The ring on Overview is a control with no name. It is the setup progress chip, ring-only on a phone. A coach cannot tell what it is until they tap it; a ring beside a title reads as “loading”.
    • Not the product: the dev server’s “N” badge overlaps the Overview tab in every capture. Nothing to fix; ignore it in the pictures.

    What I’d change

    • More becomes a real bottom sheet — full width, rising from the bar, the hot three as tiles on top (Practice plans · Lineups · Skills & Goals), then the remaining groups as 44px rows in two columns where the labels are short, Help and Sign out at the foot. Sixteen entries fit in 844 with no inner scroll. Drawn at true size on the 0 · The shell tab.
    • The masthead at rest on a phone is the one-liner (team name · record · “?”) on every screen except Overview, which keeps the two lines because it is the team’s own page. That returns 23px on every screen before anyone scrolls, and stops two headers stacking on the chat room.
    • The ring gets its number (“7/9”) or goes into More on a phone. A control that cannot be named has not earned the title row.
    Your notes on this screen
    Q 0.1

    Should More become a full-width bottom sheet with the three phone-first tools on top?

    Same sixteen entries, same six groups, same order as the desktop sidebar (the guard test that pins the two navs equal keeps holding). What changes is the container: a sheet the width of the phone with everything visible at once, instead of a 210px popover that scrolls. The three tools you named get the first row as tiles so they are one tap from anywhere.

    Recommendation: Reshape. This is the cheapest change in the walk and it fixes the thing you asked about first — whether the navigation is understandable. Drawn on the stage-0 tab.
    What rides on it: the nav-groups guard test (unchanged — same labels); the demo tour’s phone stops that open More; the help article on getting around on a phone.
    Q 0.2

    Does Roster keep its primary slot, or does one of the season’s tools take it?

    Your list of what coaches use most on a phone — chat, schedule, lineups, practice plans, overview, skills — does not include the roster, and two of the tools on it are behind More. So the question is real. My reading: the bar is right and the roads are wrong. Roster is the door to every player (the fence question is “has Devon paid, who do I call, what does he throw”), and Lineups and Practice plans are already reached from the day’s card on Overview and from the event on the Schedule — the problem is what those roads look like on a phone (stations 1 and 2), plus the sheet (Q 0.1).

    Recommendation: Keep the four, fix the three roads, and re-ask this after stage 2 ships. If the tools still feel buried then, the swap is a one-line change and we will have evidence.
    What rides on it: nothing yet — a Keep here costs nothing; a Reshape would pick which tool takes the slot and I would draw it.
    Q 0.3

    On a phone, should the masthead rest as its one-line form on every screen except Overview?

    The collapsed line already exists and already reads well (team name at the left, the record and “?” at the right). This makes it the resting state on a phone for every screen that has a page title of its own, and keeps the two-line identity on Overview. The desktop is untouched — the ruling that the desktop never collapses stands.

    Recommendation: Reshape. 23px on every screen, and the chat room stops wearing two headers.
    What rides on it: the masthead’s published height that stacked sticky elements read (it already changes on collapse, so every consumer already copes); the game-day status slot, which is already absent at phone width by ruling.
    Where I’d push on the shape

    Reshape the container, not the map. Every station below assumes the four tabs stay; if you rule Q 0.2 the other way, stations 4 and 6 get a second door and I will redraw the sheet with two tiles instead of three.

    1

    The first screen — Overview on a phone

    A coach opens the portal on game day. What do they see, and how much of it is for a phone?

    Overview …/teams/{id} · the One Thing card · the six tiles · the “Worth a look” line
    On the screen, as built

    Masthead; “Overview · U14” with the ring; the game-day card — GAME DAY · TODAY · vs Probe Rovers · Build lineup → · 2:55 p.m. · UAT Fields, Diamond 1 and six chips in two rows: 10 of 12 in · ⚠ Lineup needs review · 1 late · 1 out · Call 5:30 p.m. · Home kit; then “Your team at a glance” — six tiles two-up: Roster 12 · active players · a 0/12 bar · “12 missing email”; Record 3-2-1 · League + Tournament · W L T W L; This week 1 practice · in the next 7 days; Dues $7,349 · outstanding · 1 overdue · a bar · 10/104 paid; Budget $9,020 · $3,980 of $13,000 spent · a bar · 31%; Tournaments None yet · Register for a tournament; then “⚠ Worth a look: #12 Logan Test went over the pitching cap in 3 games” beside “Season insights →”.

    height 1,087px · 1.3 screenswords 124 · on the first screen 102at ≤11px 33 of 126 wordschips that are doors 4 × 32px“Season insights →” 22px tall

    How it feels to use — my assessment

    What works

    • The One Thing card is exactly what a phone wants: the day, the opponent, the time and place, and one lime button for the job. It is the best-designed 200px in the portal after the console.
    • The page is short. One and a third screens; nothing to hunt for. Two-up tiles keep all six figures above the second fold.
    • The “Worth a look” line is a good phone sentence — one fact, one door.

    What gets in the way

    • The tiles are desktop tiles at half width. Each carries a label, a figure, a sub-line, a bar and a note — five things in a 170px box. “TOURNAMENTS” is longer than its box and runs into its own arrow. The sub-lines (“League + Tournament”, “outstanding · 1 overdue” and “10/104 paid”) are annotations a desktop has room for; on a phone they are the 11px words that make a third of the screen’s text.
    • The chips row mixes doors with facts. Four of the six are links to attendance or the lineup and they are 32px tall — under the tap floor. Two (“Call 5:30 p.m.”, “Home kit”) are facts dressed as buttons; a coach taps them and nothing happens.
    • The bar in the Roster tile says 0/12 with no word for what is counted (positions set). A bar with no label is a decoration.

    What I’d change

    • On a phone, a tile is a row: icon · label · figure · one qualifier, 56px, the whole row the door — “Roster · 12 · 12 missing email”, “Record · 3-2-1 · W L T W L”, “Dues · $7,349 · 1 overdue”, “Budget · $9,020 left · 31% spent”. Six rows are 336px against the tiles’ 570; the arrow goes; the collision goes; the bars go (the page each row opens has the bar).
    • The card’s facts join the meta line (“2:55 p.m. · UAT Fields, Diamond 1 · call 5:30 · home kit”) and the four state chips stay as doors at 44px, two per row. Same words, same doors, one kind of thing per row.
    Your notes on this screen
    Q 1.1

    On a phone, do the six tiles become six rows — one figure, one qualifier, the row a door?

    This is the example you gave (“the dashboard tiles might need less text on mobile”), and the measurements agree: a third of the screen’s words are at the smallest steps and they are all in the tiles. Rows keep every figure and every door; what leaves is the second sub-line and the bar, which belong to the page the row opens. Desktop tiles are untouched.

    Recommendation: Reshape — stage 1, drawn at true size once stage 0 is ruled.
    What rides on it: the tile set is already computed per capability (a coach without Money sees no Dues row) — nothing changes in what is shown, only its shape; the layout sweep’s Overview screen.
    Q 1.2

    Do the card’s two facts leave the chip row, and the four doors grow to the tap floor?

    “Call 5:30 p.m.” and “Home kit” are answers, not actions; put them on the meta line with the venue. The attendance and lineup chips are the day’s second and third jobs and deserve a real tap target.

    Recommendation: Reshape, with stage 1.
    What rides on it: the game-day card’s state resolver (unchanged — it already knows which chips are doors); the baselined 32px tap-floor entries for these chips, which this fixes and prunes.

    Schedule — the list opens in April

    A coach taps Schedule in September to see what is next, and on game day opens the game to take attendance.

    Schedule …/schedule · List · Week · Month · the “+ ▾” menu · the event sheet
    On the screen, as built

    List opens at the top of the season: APRIL 2026 · vs Ridgeview 6–3 WIN · Apr 4 · 6:00 p.m. and on down — five months of results before today. The first upcoming row (today’s game with its Game day pill) sits at 1,345px, a screen and a half down, on every open. Week opens on this week and draws all seven days as 150px cards, four of them empty (“—”). Month draws the grid with event chips cut to UAT … and Practi…. The “+ ▾” menu lists six event types and is good. The event sheet (a full-screen sheet with a real back) for today’s game runs: LEAGUE GAME · name · when · where · “+ Add final score” · AWARDS GIVEN (locked until a score) · a “Share game link” card with four lines of copy and a Share button · Edit details · Cancel event · Delete · then the tabs Attendance · Lineup · Scouting · then All in / Reset / Season attendance · the count chips · the first player’s In / Edit RSVP at about 1,150px.

    list height 1,718px · 2.0 screensfirst upcoming row at 1,345pxweek: empty days 4 × ~150pxsheet: first player at ~1,150px

    How it feels to use — my assessment

    What works

    • The rows are right for a thumb: two lines, the type icon, the result at the right, the whole row a door. The month headings keep you oriented.
    • The add menu is one tap to six event types with their icons — a coach at the field can add Tuesday’s practice in three taps.
    • The event sheet is a real phone sheet: full-screen, a back arrow, 44px rows; attendance’s All in and per-row Edit RSVP are easy to hit.

    What gets in the way

    • The list opens on the past. The Practice plans and Lineups rooms both learned this month to open on the next one and band the rest as “coming up” and “recent”; the Schedule, the screen a coach opens most, still starts at the first game of the year. On a phone that is 1.6 screens of thumb every time.
    • Week draws nothing four times. Four empty 150px cards is 600px of “—” before Friday.
    • Month cannot say what is on a day. A 45px cell holds three letters; the chips are unreadable, and tapping a day opens nothing.
    • The sheet’s order is the desktop’s. On the day, attendance and the lineup are the job; a final score, awards and a share link are for afterwards; delete is for never. The phone puts the job at 1,150px.

    What I’d change

    • The list opens on today — the next event at the top under a “Coming up” heading, the season so far folded above it as one row (“Earlier this season · 12 events”), which opens in place. Same rows, same data.
    • Week collapses empty days to one quiet line (“Mon–Thu · nothing scheduled”) so the week is the two cards that have something in them.
    • Month on a phone = dots on the grid + the tapped day’s rows beneath it (the way every phone calendar does it). Today is pre-selected.
    • The sheet follows the day: for today and upcoming events the tabs come first (Attendance · Lineup · Scouting), then the details; for a finished game the score comes first; Share · Edit · Cancel · Delete become one quiet row at the foot. Same content, ordered by when it is needed.
    Your notes on this screen
    Q 2.1

    Should the Schedule list open on today, with the season so far folded above?

    The practice and lineup rooms already answer “what is next” at the top. This applies the same rule to the list a coach opens most. Desktop gets it too — a September desktop scrolls past the spring as well, just with a mouse.

    Recommendation: Reshape — stage 2. Every width.
    What rides on it: the deep links that open a specific event (unchanged — they open the sheet, not the list); the demo tour’s schedule stop (its anchor is a row, and the row survives); the export (whole season, unchanged).
    Q 2.2

    Should Week and Month be redrawn for a phone — empty days collapsed, month as dots plus a day list?

    Two views that make sense on a wide screen and lose their meaning at 390. Week keeps its structure and drops its blanks; Month keeps the grid and gains the list a phone needs to read it.

    Recommendation: Reshape — stage 2, phone widths only.
    What rides on it: nothing off the Schedule page.
    Q 2.3

    On a phone, should the event sheet order itself by the day — tabs first before and on the day, score first after?

    The sheet has the right parts; a phone needs them in the order they are used. This is the road from Schedule to attendance and the lineup, and it is the one that puts the job at 1,150px today.

    Recommendation: Reshape — stage 2. Same on the desktop’s drawer if you want one order; I would keep it phone-only first and see.
    What rides on it: the sheet’s deep links (?event=…&tab=attendance) — they select a tab and still work; the finished-season reader never opens this sheet.

    Chat — two headers over the room

    The most phone-shaped thing a coach does: read a message from the assistant and answer it.

    Chat …/chat · “Your chats” · a room
    On the screen, as built

    The list — “YOUR CHATS” with the “?”, then a card per room: avatar, name, “Your coaching staff”, the last line, a STAFF tag. It lists every room this person is in, across their teams: on this fixture the head coach of UAT Test Team sees UAT Standalone Team (No Metrics) staff and UAT Standalone Team staff — two other teams’ rooms — under a tab that sits inside UAT Test Team. The room — the masthead stays pinned (59px); a room header below it (61px: the name cut to “UAT Standalone Team (No Metrics) s…”, “Your coaching staff”, a ‹ back button on the right beside the “?”); the messages; the composer (emoji · poll · “Write a message…” · send) clear of the bar.

    pinned above the messages 120pxpinned below 132pxfor messages 592px · 70%rooms listed 2, neither this team’s

    How it feels to use — my assessment

    What works

    • It reads like a messaging app. The room fills the screen, the composer sits on the bar, a single room opens itself, the send button is lime.
    • The cards are big and tappable and the unread count is on the tab.

    What gets in the way

    • Two headers. The masthead says the team, the room header says the room; on a phone that is 120px before the first message, and the room’s name is the one that gets cut.
    • Back is on the right. Every other screen in the portal puts back at the left; here it sits beside the “?”, where the eye expects a close.
    • A per-person list under a per-team tab. One-team coaches never notice. A coach on three teams (a club coach, a parent-coach) opens Chat under Team A and reads Team B’s room first — the list is sorted by activity, not by where you are standing.

    What I’d change

    • On a phone the room owns its header — the masthead does not render over an open room (the bar still says where you are, the room header says which room). With Q 0.3 this is a one-line masthead gone, not two.
    • Back on the left, the “?” alone on the right.
    • This team’s rooms first, then an “Other teams” rule and the rest. Same list, ordered by where the coach is.
    Your notes on this screen
    Q 3.1

    On a phone, should an open room drop the masthead and put back on the left?

    The room header is the identity here; the masthead is a second one. Back moves to where every other phone screen keeps it.

    Recommendation: Reshape — stage 5 (people), or fold it into stage 0 since it rides on the masthead rule. I have drawn it with stage 0 as A2’s second frame.
    What rides on it: the chat height variables the room sets for itself (it already cancels the page padding — it would cancel the masthead the same way); nothing on the desktop.
    Q 3.2

    Should the list put this team’s rooms first?

    Cheap, and only visible to multi-team coaches — which is the club segment. One rule (“the team you are standing in sorts first”), no new data.

    Recommendation: Reshape — stage 5.
    What rides on it: the consumer chat inbox is separate and untouched.

    Lineups — a screen of setup before the first player

    On the bus, a coach opens Saturday’s lineup to move a pitcher out of inning 5.

    Lineups …/lineups (the room) · the builder …/lineups/{game} · Playing time
    On the screen, as built

    The room (brought level with Practice plans yesterday): Games · Templates tabs, the GAME DAY card with Open game day in lime and Open lineup beneath, then RECENT GAMES rows with their “Needs review” chips — 1,021px and easy. The builder: back · “vs Probe Rovers” · the date and View on schedule · Lineup | Playing time · the NEEDS REVIEW strip (one banner, one door — built yesterday) · SETUP: Format select · Innings select · Auto-fill · Balanced ▾ · Reshuffle · undo · redo · print · Templates ▾ — eight controls over five rows, three of them a control beside empty air · the hint “Hold a number to move a player · swipe across innings →” · the grid at 788px: BAT · PLAYER pinned, two innings per screen (seven innings = four swipes), 12 rows of 58px, a select per cell · Clear positions · NOT IN THE LINEUP · notes. The ✓ Saved pill floats at the bottom right, over the grid’s last visible cells.

    height 1,917px · 2.3 screenscontrols 118the grid begins at 788pxgrid 680px wide in 356 · 2 of 7 innings per screensetup rows 5 for 8 controls

    How it feels to use — my assessment

    What works

    • The grid is a genuine phone surface: 44px-plus cells, the player pinned while innings swipe, the number to reorder — the tablet-band work and the phone rules it inherited are right.
    • The strip says what is wrong in one line and opens the check; Playing time reads cleanly as a list.
    • The room is the practice room’s cousin and the phone is fine with it.

    What gets in the way

    • A full screen of setup before the first player. Format, innings and auto-fill are chosen once; undo, redo and print are desktop-week tools; on a phone the coach came to change one cell. Three of the five setup rows are a control beside empty space because the controls wrap one at a time.
    • “Saved” floats over the work. A pill at the bottom right of a phone is over the grid’s cells and, on Practice plans, over the sheet’s last line. It is a fact, not a control, and it needs a fixed home.

    What I’d change

    • Setup folds on a phone once a lineup exists — one row that reads its own state (“Everyone bats · 7 innings · Auto-fill: Balanced ▾”) and opens the controls when tapped. A new lineup opens with it unfolded.
    • Undo · redo · print · templates become one icon row, four 44px squares across, under the strip.
    • “Saved” becomes transient. A pill that appears on an edit, says “✓ Saved” and fades about two seconds after the save lands; only a failure stays. The same piece on every screen that autosaves (stage 0, A3 — revised 20 Sep: the title row was drawn first and retired on the desktop read, because the title row is pinned nowhere).
    Your notes on this screen
    Q 4.1

    On a phone, does Setup fold into one self-describing row once a lineup exists?

    The grid starts at about 330px instead of 788 — the first six players on the first screen. Nothing is removed; the controls are one tap further for the one visit in twenty that needs them.

    Recommendation: Reshape — stage 3 (game week).
    What rides on it: the template editor shares the setup block and gets the same fold; the demo tour’s lineup stop (an anchor on the grid, unchanged).
    Q 4.2

    Do undo, redo, print and templates become one icon row on a phone?

    Four squares, 44px each, one row. Same four actions; the labels the desktop shows are the tooltips here, and a coach met them on the desktop first (the icon-only rule).

    Recommendation: Reshape — stage 3, with Q 4.1.
    What rides on it: the page-actions guard test, which enumerates this header.

    Game day — the console is the reference screen

    At the fence, in daylight, one hand: who is on the field this inning, who has sat longest, what is the score.

    Game day …/game/{event} · from the Overview card, the Lineups room and the masthead’s live window
    On the screen, as built

    ← SCHEDULE · GAME DAY · ✓ SAVED; the pinned card — vs Probe Rovers › · Home, four chips (1 · Arrive 5:30 p.m. · Home kit · Screen staying on), US — THEM over two dash inputs, ‹ INNING 1 OF 7 ›; ON THE FIELD — INNING 1 as 44px rows (number · name · “1 of 2 innings pitched” · position); BENCH — LONGEST SITTING FIRST; a pinned action bar. 1,290px; 27 controls; nothing under the tap floor.

    height 1,290px · 1.5 screenswords at 10–11px 66 of 122 · 54%controls under 44px 0

    How it feels to use — my assessment

    What works

    • This is the screen every other phone screen should be measured against. Rows a thumb cannot miss, the score pinned, the inning stepper where the thumb rests, the bench sorted by who has sat longest, a screen-stay chip because someone thought about a phone in a pocket.
    • Nothing under the tap floor, and no sideways scroll at 360.

    What gets in the way

    • More than half its words are set at the two smallest steps — the position letters (RF, P, C at 11px), the pitching count (“1 of 2 innings pitched” at 10px), the section labels, the score’s own label. The type ladder is right and these steps exist; this screen is the one place they are read standing up, in sun, at arm’s length.
    • The chip that says “1” is the field number and reads as a count. “US — THEM” over two dashes is a score nobody has entered yet, drawn like a score.

    What I’d change

    • A field floor: on the screens read standing up — the console, the run screen, attendance-taking — nothing the coach reads is below 12px and the thing they look for (the position, the name, the score) is at body or above. A token, not a per-screen fix.
    • “Diamond 1” instead of “1”; “0 – 0 · tap to score” until a run is entered.
    Your notes on this screen
    Q 5.1

    Should there be a field floor — 12px minimum, positions at body size — on the screens a coach reads standing up?

    The ladder stays eight steps. This says which of them the field is allowed to use, and it is enforced the way the tap floor is: a rule per surface, checked by the layout sweep.

    Recommendation: Reshape — stage 0, A4 (it is a token, and stage 0 is where the tokens are). Drawn as a true-size specimen on the stage-0 tab.
    What rides on it: the console, the run screen, the event sheet’s attendance list; the layout sweep gains a rule; the type-scale ruling is untouched.

    Practice plans — the toolbar before the sheet

    How it feels to use — my assessment

    What works

    • The room and the run screen are phone screens. The card answers “when and is there a plan”, the list answers “where am I” — both in one screen, both with the lime where the thumb is.
    • The sheet reads top to bottom and its rows open in place; the record’s read face is text, not greyed inputs.

    What gets in the way

    • Four equal buttons before the sheet. On a phone the plan is opened to read or to run; Save as template and Print the sheet are desk actions. They take 110px and the same weight as Run.
    • The Saved pill again, over the last line of the sheet.

    What I’d change

    • On a phone the toolbar is Run practice (full width on the day, plain otherwise) and a “⋯” that holds Save as template · Print the sheet · Send to staff. 44px, one row.
    • Saved → a transient pill (stage 0, A3, revised).

The session — the header wraps the session’s name over three lines; the when line; “12 players · 4 tests · 1 skill · Change ›”; a test select; “what you saw · 3 descriptors”; then the twelve players, each as name · Saved/Not recorded · Mark not assessed over a “Record an observation ›” button — three rows a player; the count (“2 recorded · 0 not assessed · 10 not recorded”) and Review session → at the very foot — 1,971px.

    How it feels to use — my assessment

    What works

    • The hub’s three cards say the state in one figure each, and Needs attention is the right thing to read while checking in from a phone.
    • The session page is honest — every player, what is and is not recorded, and a summary before the review.

    What gets in the way

    • The header breaks the phone rule. Every other create is a lime “+” in the title row; here it is a word button on a row of its own.
    • Recording is built for a desk. A coach at practice records one test for whoever is in front of them; the page asks for scroll · tap · dialog · save · back, twelve times, with the tally and the Review door at the very bottom.
    • The session’s name is three lines of title. The when line under it says the same date.

    What I’d change

    • “+” in the title row, like the others.
    • On a phone a player is one 56px row (name · state) and the row is the door; the dialog’s save offers Next player, so twelve players is twelve taps and no scrolling.
    • The tally and Review session dock above the bar (the practice plan’s docked-bar idiom) so the count is always in view and the way out is under the thumb.
    • The title is the session’s name on one line; the date lives on the when line only.

    Standing back — seven rules across the walk

    Seven things that are true at every station. Rule these and most of the station questions above are decided with them; that is the order I would take them in.

    S.1 · The bar is right; the roads are wrong

    Is the navigation understandable? Yes — and the season’s tools are still hard to reach, because the three roads to them were drawn for a desktop.

    The bottom bar’s four words are plain and a coach learns them in a minute. What they cannot learn is that Practice plans is under More, under the fold of a 210px popover; that the day’s lineup is two rows of 32px chips on a card; that attendance on the day is 1,150px into the event sheet. Fix the More sheet (Q 0.1), the card (Q 1.2) and the sheet’s order (Q 2.3) before touching the tabs (Q 0.2).

    S.2 · The screen budget

    Should a phone screen pin at most one identity line — a budget of about 110px at rest, not 131 — and never two headers?

    The masthead at rest as its one-liner (Q 0.3) and the chat room owning its header (Q 3.1) both follow from this. It is a rule the layout sweep can hold, the way it holds the tap floor.

    S.3 · Today first

    Should every list that mixes past and future open on today, with the past folded above?

    The practice and lineup rooms do; the Schedule does not (Q 2.1); the Insights sessions list opens on the newest. One rule, and the Schedule is the last exception.

    S.4 · One figure, one qualifier

    On a phone, does a summary tile or card carry a label, a figure and one line — and nothing else?

    Overview’s tiles (Q 1.1), the Skills & Goals cards (already close), Money’s summary band. What is cut is not information; it is on the page the tile opens. This is the direct answer to “are we displaying too much on mobile” — the tiles are, the cards mostly are not.

    S.5 · The field floor

    On the screens read standing up, is 12px the smallest size and the thing looked for at body size or above?

    The console (Q 5.1), the run screen, attendance-taking. A token and a sweep rule; the ladder is untouched.

    S.6 · Where “Saved” lives

    Does “Saved” show only while it has something to say — and stay only when a save fails?

    The lineup builder, the practice plan, the attendance list and Playing time all float the same pill over their own bottom-right corner, permanently. Drawn first as a word in the title row (stage-0 tab, A3); revised 20 Sep on the desktop read — the title row is pinned nowhere, so the word scrolled away with it. The pill stays, but only while a save is pending or has just landed.

    S.7 · A table stays a table

    When a table’s columns fit at 390, does it stay a table on a phone?

    Attendance (Q 9.1) is the case in hand; the stacked-card idiom stays for the tables that genuinely do not fit. The row-list recipe already says this for lists; this says it for reports.

    The stages, as I would take them

    One at a time, each drawn at true size on its own tab before it is built, each with its own QA walk. Stage 0 is drawn now.

    1. 0The shell — More as a bottom sheet with the hot three on top; the masthead at rest as one line (and gone over a chat room); “Saved” as a transient pill; the field floor as a token; the ring named. Stations 0, 3 (half), 5; S.2, S.5, S.6.
    2. 1The first screen — the six tiles as six rows; the card’s facts to the meta line and its doors to 44px. Station 1; S.4.
    3. 2Schedule — today first with the past folded; week without blanks; month as dots plus a day list; the event sheet ordered by the day. Station 2; S.3.
    4. 3Game week — the builder’s setup folded, the tool row as icons. Station 4.
    5. 4Practice week & skills — the plan’s one-row toolbar; recording as rows with Next player and a docked tally; the “+”. Stations 6, 7.
    6. 5People — the player’s read face with Edit; prev/next; the chat list this-team-first. Stations 3 (half), 8; after §182 is walked.
    7. 6Reports — tables that fit stay tables; short tab labels; the notification clamp. Stations 9, 10; S.7.

    Design intent. A confirmation is a moment, not furniture: the common autosave pattern is a word that appears while something is happening and leaves once it has. The three honest states stay (“Unsaved changes” while edits wait for the debounce, “Saving…” while a request is open, “✓ Saved” when it lands), and because the pill is pinned to the window it is in the same corner wherever the page is scrolled — the property the title row could not give. The failure is the exception by design: “Couldn’t save · Retry” holds its place until a retry lands, so a coach can never keep editing a lineup that stopped saving three innings ago. Restyled when the pill is on screen · Unchanged where it sits and what it says.

    Design intent. The name is already the one word on every screen; a chevron says it is also a door, the way TeamSnap’s and TeamLinkt’s team titles do. The sheet is the More sheet’s own container and rows (52px, tinted current, the closed team’s season name as its quiet qualifier), rising from the bar so the thumb reaches it — never a dropdown hanging under the name. The tap target is the whole name plus the chevron, 44px tall through the same 4px overhang the “?” already uses above and below the 36px line; the bar does not grow. Proved in the browser, not asserted: on today’s slim line the record and the “?” keep their places while the name gives way — “UAT Between Seasons” (154px of text) and “Riverdale Ridge 12U Mustangs” (206px) both fit beside a chevron at 390 and 360; a longer name truncates with an ellipsis before the chevron, so the chevron is never the thing that disappears (the six specimens above are live CSS, not pictures — the third line truncates for real). The Overview’s two-line form takes the chevron on its first line. The closed-season page’s line reads “UAT Between Seasons ⌄ · ?”, which is what it reads today minus the chevron: on a phone a finished season’s masthead names nothing — “Complete” and “Final 2-1-1” are in the page but hidden with the whole status slot under 640px (the 24 August ruling), which the walk did not record. Not restored here: the page beneath says “2025 Season” in its title, in Season Wrapped and in the bar’s single tab. New the chevron and the sheet · Restyled More without the switcher block (497px, was 630) · Unchanged the rows themselves, the desktop select, the single-team name.

    B1

    The team switcher is a chevron on the team name (2+ teams) opening a bottom sheet of the one-list rows; the rows leave More

    Same rows, new door. More becomes tools only and its tiles sit 133px higher; the slim line stays 36px with a 44px tap.

    B2 · The masthead — two lines that thin, or one line everywhere Recommended: B Ruled: B · 21 Sep

    On the walk you asked for the Overview’s masthead — two lines that thin as you scroll — on every screen, for consistency. Drawn as A below. My recommendation is the opposite, B: the one 36px line stage 0 gave every other screen, on the Overview too, with the Overview’s “club · season” line kept exactly where it is at rest but as page content under the pinned line — it scrolls away like everything else instead of snapping. Both are drawn at true size, at rest and scrolled; the numbers are measured on today’s product. You rule.

    The argument, from what the code does. (1) The collapse is a threshold toggle with hysteresis — collapse past 64px of scroll, expand under 12 — so it does not shrink, it snaps 59→36: the content under the thumb jumps 23px, and jumps back on the way up. Measured today at 390 and 360: scroll 63 → 59px bar; scroll 65 → 36px bar. (2) The collapsed form hides the whole right slot, the “?” included; stage 0’s slim line was built precisely so a tool screen keeps its “?” through scroll. Drawn honestly, A’s thin form must keep the “?” and the record — and that form is the slim line we already have. A is therefore “add a second line at rest to every tool screen, and take it away again past 64px”. (3) What the second line carries on a tool screen is the club and the season. The record is already on the slim line; the season has one value a coach cannot change (no season dial, by ruling); a standalone team has no club, so its second line is just “2026 Season”. Two words, for 22px of first-screen content on every tool screen — the lineup grid, the run sheet, the console. (4) TeamSnap’s shrinking large title is the page title, which this portal already draws as the title row under the masthead; A puts two things in motion above the content. B keeps the club its home — it is named nowhere else on a phone since the 2026-08-17 slimdown — as the Overview’s own first line, in the same place and words as today, only unpinned. On the tablet band (641–900) the collapse exists on every screen today; B removes it there too, which is the 2026-08-19 “the bar stays put” ruling reaching down from the desktop. Desktop untouched under both. Recommended B · Restyled the Overview’s masthead (B) or every tool screen’s (A) · Unchanged the desktop, the words, the “?”.

    B2

    The masthead on a phone: A — two lines that thin on scroll, on every screen (the ask) · B — one 36px line on every screen, the Overview’s club · season line as page content (recommended)

    Either way the masthead behaves the same on every screen, which is the consistency you asked for. They differ in what the consistency costs: A spends 22px of every tool screen and a 22px jump per scroll; B spends nothing and keeps the “?” in view.

    B3 · The six tiles become six rows

    Same six things, same doors, same capability gating (a coach without Money sees no Dues row), same order — the shape changes. A row is a label with one qualifier under it, the figure on the right, a chevron; 52px; the whole row is the door. The qualifier is the tile’s warning when it has one (“12 missing email”), otherwise its sub-line; the bars, the second sub-lines and the arrows leave, because the page each row opens has them. Desktop tiles untouched.

    Design intent. A tile at half width carries five things in a 170px box; a row carries three and reads left to right the way a list does. Every figure a tile shows today is on its row, in the tile’s own words: Roster · 12 · 12 missing email, Record · 3-2-1 · W L T W L, This week · 1 practice · in the next 7 days, Dues · $7,349 · outstanding · 1 overdue (the danger tone on the figure), Budget · $9,020 · $3,980 of $13,000 spent, Tournaments · None yet · Register for a tournament (the muted tone: words at heading size, as the tile does). The number sits at the title step in the display face, one step down from the tile’s figure; a words-figure at heading; the label at body; the qualifier at support — the ladder’s own steps, no ninth size. Measured on the drawing: six rows at 52 with 6px gaps are 342px against the board’s 520 — 178px back — and all six sit above the bar at 390×844, the sixth ending 4px clear of it (on the 780-tall Android the sixth is a short scroll down). 52 is the sheet’s own row height and well over the 44px floor; the walk said 56, and at 56 the sixth row’s foot sat 20px under the bar — the frame decided. The board’s seven eyebrow words at 11px go to 14; with B the masthead’s six meta words go to 12 as the page line, so the page’s 33 words at ≤11px become 20 — the bar’s five labels, the kicker, the card’s kicker and the five pips, all recognised rather than read. The page as drawn is about 900px tall against 1,104 today. One correction to the walk: “TOURNAMENTS collides with its arrow” does not reproduce on today’s tree — it clears by 23px at 390 and 9px at 360; the rows remove the arrow regardless. Restyled six tiles as six rows at ≤640 · Unchanged the tile set, its order, every figure, every door, the desktop board, the setup ring.

    B3

    On a phone the six tiles are six 52px rows — label, one qualifier, the figure, the whole row a door; bars and second lines leave

    B4 · The card’s facts join the meta line; its doors grow to 44px

    “Call 5:30 p.m.” and “Home kit” are answers, not actions — a coach taps them and nothing happens — so they join the meta line beside the venue. The attendance and lineup chips are the day’s second and third jobs and get a real target. One deviation from Q 1.2’s “four doors, two per row”: three of the four door-chips (“10 of 12 in”, “1 late”, “1 out”) open the same page, so the drawing has two doors, one per destination, each a full-width 44px row in the same row idiom as B3 — the attendance door carrying its three counts as one sentence, the lineup door its state. Same words, same colours, same state resolver.

    Design intent. One kind of thing per row: the meta line is facts (time, place, call time, kit), the doors are jobs. A door names its state in its colour — green with a check when the job is done, amber with a warning when it is not — exactly as the chips do today, and a door only renders for a coach who holds that duty (the card’s resolver is unchanged: it already knows which chips are doors, and a chip it does not offer is a door that is not drawn). When attendance has not been taken the first door reads “⚠ Attendance not taken” on its own; the late, out and no-reply counts appear only once it has, inside that door. Measured on the drawing: the card grows from 225px to 256 at 390 — two 44px doors where two 32px chip rows were, and the meta line wrapping to a second line to hold the facts — and B3 gives back 178, so the first screen nets 147px ahead. The baselined 32px tap-floor entries for these four chips are pruned with the build. Restyled the chip row as two doors, the facts on the meta line · Unchanged the kicker, the headline, the lime action, the resolver, the desktop card.

    B4

    “Call 5:30 p.m.” and “Home kit” move to the meta line; the attendance and lineup chips become two 44px doors, one per destination

    B5 · The rows’ ground — the board came out grey; the drawing was white ruled B · built 21 Sep

    Your read of the built screen: “why are these tiles grey? isn’t that a little dull?” It is, and it was not a decision. The B3 drawing above drew the six rows white — the desktop tile’s own skin. The build rendered them through the portal’s one row component (the right call — one row recipe, not a second one), and on a phone that component paints every row with the table’s row-as-card wash: olive at 10 % over the cream paper, which composites to #E8E6D8 — a greenish grey that is neither the paper nor a card. That wash is right for a stack of records — fifteen roster rows, a month of schedule — where quiet is the point. It was never meant for six doors carrying the coach’s own numbers under a white hero card. So the default leaked, and the fix to the drawing is owed either way. Two grounds drawn at true size, beside the built one; the only thing that changes between the three frames is the ground.

    Why it reads dull, precisely. Three things, not one. (1) It is a tint. Olive at 10 % over the paper is neither the paper nor a card; it is the “washed row” the table standard retired from every desktop table in July (F-10) for exactly this reason, kept only as the phone’s row-card so a long list stays quiet. (2) Six identical slabs. Nothing separates one row from the next but a gap, and nothing separates the band from the paper around it — the eye has no edge to land on. (3) The screen inverts. The game-day card above is white and lifted; the board under it sinks into the paper, so the first screen goes from “one thing” to “one thing, then beige”. The desktop has none of this: its six tiles are white door cards with a hairline and a whisper of shadow, and the drawing carried that skin down.

    A · six white cards — the B3 drawing as you approved it. The desktop tile’s own skin at row height: white, the neutral hairline, 10px corners, a whisper of shadow, 6px between cards, 52px rows. Six separate doors, which is what six separate tiles are on the desktop. It is the fix that is owed regardless; nothing about it needs a new ruling.

    B · one framed list — recommended, and argued from the walk’s own rule. The same six rows inside one white frame, a hairline between rows, no gaps: the shape every row list already has on the desktop, kept at phone width. Your rule S.7 from the walk — a table whose columns fit stays a table — is the argument: the phone’s row-as-card form exists for tables whose columns do not fit, and this board’s three columns (label with its qualifier · the figure · the chevron) fit at 390 and at 360. Three things follow. The figures line up. Six numbers in one right-hand column read as a column of numbers — a scoreboard — where six cards with gaps read as six separate sentences. Room comes back. Five gaps and ten card edges leave; measured on the drawings, the band goes from 342px to 314 — 28px back — and the sixth row’s foot from 4px clear of the bar to 33px clear. On the built page, whose rows are 49, that is today’s 5px becoming about 33 — the margin the B3 drawing had to trade 56px rows for 52 to find. One shape under the hero. The game-day card, then one quiet white block, then the bridge line; the card stays the one thing. The risk, named: B would be the first row list in the portal that stays framed on a phone, so it is a second phone-list form — justified only by S.7 and by this board not being a list of records. Every other list (roster, schedule, the money rooms) keeps its row-cards; nothing there changes.

    Two options considered and not drawn. Colour the marks — a tinted disc behind each row’s icon (olive for Roster, green for Record, red for Dues…). Rejected: in this palette colour carries state, never category (the game-day card is green-edged because the game is today, not because it is a game); six coloured discs would be the only place in the portal where a category wears a colour, and the ground would still be beige. Lighten the wash — the 8 % fill instead of the 10 % olive. Rejected: a lighter tint is still a tint; the tables retired the tint, not its strength. Restyled the six rows’ ground at ≤640, and only that · Unchanged the tile set, its order, every figure, every qualifier, every door, the desktop board, and every other row list’s phone card.

    B5

    The board’s rows on a phone: A — six white cards, the B3 drawing as approved · B — one white framed list, the figures in a column (recommended)

    Either way the grey goes and the six rows keep their words, figures and doors. They differ in shape: A is six doors with air between them, the desktop’s six tiles read as a list; B is one framed list, the walk’s S.7 applied to the one list on the phone whose columns fit.

    Ruled B (owner, in the chat, 21 September) and built the same session: the list declares the recipe’s framed phone form; the recipe carries that form once, after the stand-down it overrides; the rendered sweep reads the declaration and holds the list to it. Measured on the built page at 390×844: one white frame, hairlines, rows 48–49px, the band 287px against 324, the sixth row’s foot 40px clear of the bar (was 5); the page 916px against 948. At 360×780 the sixth row ends 57px under the bar (was 92) — the short scroll the drawing allowed. Nothing else on the phone changed; every other list keeps its row-cards; the desktop is untouched.

    B6 · Breathing room — the frame is right; the rows inside it are still cut to the old constraint ruled B · built 21 Sep

    Your read of the built B5: “does it feel a little squished and cluttered?” Yes, and both halves have a cause. Squished: the rows are 48px with two lines of text and 5–6px of padding above and below — a density B3 cut on purpose to fit six gapped cards above the bar. B5 took the gaps away and won 40px back, and I left that as empty paper under the list instead of giving it back to the rows. Cluttered: every row carries five things — an icon, the label, a caption, the figure, a chevron — 35 elements in 287px; the six icons are a column of glyphs saying what the six words beside them already say, and two of the six captions are not facts about your team but a definition (“in the next 7 days”) and an instruction (“Register for a tournament”). Two ways out, drawn beside the built one; the frame, the doors, the figures and the order do not change in either.

    A · breathe. Nothing leaves. Each row goes from 48px to 52px — the number the B3 drawing promised and the build never reached — and the two text lines get a hair of air between them. That spends most of what B5 won: on the built page’s own geometry (the band starts at 446, the bar at 772) six 52px rows end about 13px clear of the bar. Less squished; every bit as busy.

    B · breathe and declutter — recommended. The same 52px rows, and three things leave. The icons go. Six words — Roster, Record, This week, Dues, Budget, Tournaments — need no glyph to be recognised, and without the column the label sits on the frame’s own edge; the desktop tiles keep theirs (an eyebrow on a card is a different job from a word in a list). The small line under a row is for a fact about your team — a warning (“12 missing email”), the record, a money qualifier (“outstanding · 1 overdue”, “$3,980 of $13,000 spent”) — never a definition or an instruction. “in the next 7 days” and “Register for a tournament” leave, and those two rows drop to one line at 44px; the rows with something to say stand out because the ones with nothing to add stay quiet. The figures step down one weight (extra-bold to bold) — still the loudest thing on each row, no longer shouting across all six. Result on the built geometry: the band about 297px, the sixth row roughly 29px clear, and 23 elements where there were 35. What it costs, named: the phone rows and the desktop tiles now differ in one more way (no icons); an empty-state row (“Tournaments · None yet”) loses its nudge — the page it opens carries the register door in the first fold, and a glance list is not where a call to action lives (the walk’s S.4: one figure, one qualifier). The rule for which captions stay is written into the tiles, not guessed from their words.

    Restyled row height and line air (both) · the icon column, two captions, the figure weight (B only) · Unchanged the frame, the six rows and their order, every figure and door, every warning caption, the record’s pips, the desktop board.

    Design intent — the list is the scroller. Your ask was “open on today’s date, not open then scroll; slide up for the past, down for the future; the header pins.” On a page that scrolls as a page, that puts the page title and the “+ ▾” above the past — the coach’s most common write would be fifteen rows up — and pinning the title row is the one thing you have ruled out for good. So the drawing uses the construction the chat room already has on a phone: the list is the thing that scrolls, between the title row and the bar; the month header pins at its top; it opens positioned on today before it paints (no scroll to watch); “+” and the view menu never move. What decides “today”: the first row dated on or after the club-local day — a game that started an hour ago is still today’s and is the first row; on a day with nothing, the next event is the first row. The end of the season leaves room beneath the last row so the last month can still reach the top (the empty paper under October is honest — the season ends there). New the pinned month header, the scroller, the view menu, the export row · Unchanged the rows’ words, the month bands, the sheet on tap, the deep links (they open the sheet), the export itself (the same three file types), the “+ ▾” menu, Week and Month (C2 — they live in the same scroller).

    The view button — icon-only, no chevron (your read, 21 September). A 44 × 44 button beside “+ ▾”, a glyph and nothing else, the way your phone’s calendar does it; it opens a three-row menu (each row with its glyph and word, a tick on the current one). Which glyph: the row’s left-hand icon is already a calendar, so a second fixed calendar glyph on the right says “calendar” twice and nothing about the view; drawn as recommended is a glyph that shows the current view — list lines, week columns, month grid — one symbol saying where you are and that it switches (Outlook’s phone calendar does this). The fixed calendar glyph is on the strip beneath as the alternative; either is one glyph in a 44px box, so nothing else on the row moves. For assistive tech the button is named “Change view · List” and the menu rows are radio items. The cost is honest: switching views is one tap further than a toggle; the gain is 59px on every open, one fewer row of chrome, and 21px of the title row back against the worded button. The “+” loses its chevron too (your read): the lime square is the add door on every list in the portal, and its six-type menu is unchanged behind it — phone only; the desktop’s worded “+ Add event ▾” keeps its chevron. Two things ride with it: the export button leaves the toolbar it shared with the toggle and becomes a quiet “Export the season ›” row at the foot of the list (the same three-choice picker behind it); and Roster’s List / Depth chart toggle stays a toggle — two options do not earn a menu (your 24 August rule against a dropdown that says less than the row it replaces). The desktop keeps its toolbar and toggle, as ruled 11 August. Restyled the view switcher and the export door at ≤640 · Unchanged the desktop toolbar, Roster’s toggle.

    The frame, and no gaps. You asked whether the spaces around the rows are needed; they are not. The Overview’s rows became one white framed list under B5 and the walk’s own rule S.7 says a list whose columns fit stays a list; the schedule’s rows fit — name and result on one line, the date under it — so they take the same declared frame: a hairline between rows, no card gaps, the month header a band inside the frame that pins as you slide. Each row comes back 11px shorter (58 against 69) and the frame gives the pinned header a ground. On game day the Game day pill still marks today’s row; on any other day the first row under the pinned header is simply the next event. Restyled the rows’ ground at ≤640 · Unchanged every row’s words, the pill, the trail.

    The desktop, restated. The first draft argued for today-first at every width because the fold row was width-agnostic. An inner scroller is a phone form; the desktop equivalent is “the page opens scrolled to today” — the same title-above-the-past cost at a mouse’s pace (on the fixture the desktop’s today row is at 815, the last row of the first screen). Recommended: phone first — the desktop keeps April at open and is re-asked once the phone is walked. The demo’s Season-start stop lands on this page with a narration line (“three games played”) and no anchor — nothing breaks at build; the next /demos pass re-reads that sentence on a list that opens on today.

    Design intent — Week. The week keeps its structure and drops its blanks: the seven-day order still reads top to bottom, and a run of empty days is one sentence instead of four cards, so the week is the two days that have something in them. A day with events is the card as built (the chip with its colour rail — K-21 keeps the rail in the calendar cell; the Game day pill stacked under it as today). The ‹ › buttons are 32px today — not in any baseline because the sweep never opens Week — and go to 44. Month. The grid stays a grid; what changes is what a cell says: a dot per event in the event type’s colour (a ticked game keeps its outlined shape, as the chip does), today’s number ringed, the selected day filled, and the day’s rows beneath the grid in the list’s row shape with a time lead (the date is the heading). Today is pre-selected on open; tapping any cell selects it — a day with nothing shows one quiet line (“Nothing on Tuesday, September 22”) and the cell stays the tap. The day sheet that “+N more” opens today is not needed on a phone once the day’s rows live under the grid; the desktop’s month keeps it. Day numbers go 11 → 12px and the weekday heads 10 → 11 — two steps on the ladder, no new size. Restyled Week’s empty days, Month’s cells, the ‹ › buttons · New the day’s rows under the grid · Unchanged the desktop’s Week and Month, the day cards with events, the “+ ▾” menu, the chips’ colours.     Design intent — the order. The sheet has the right parts; a phone needs them in the order they are used, and “the day” is decided by the clock the product already keeps. Before first pitch — an upcoming game, or today’s until it starts — the tabs sit directly under the title and the where-line: attendance, the lineup, the scouting book are the job, and they are the first thing under the thumb. The score door still exists, quietly, at the foot (a coach who types a score early finds it). From first pitch on the score leads: “+ Add final score” in the place the scoreline will hold, then the awards, then the tabs — the same order as a finished game today. Why the START and not “finished”: the walk said “score first for a finished game”; keyed on whether a score exists, the coach entering it for the first time on game night would scroll past twelve attendance rows to reach the door — the one moment the score is the job. The game-day console and the lineup’s Ready state already turn on the same start time, so the sheet turns with them. Practices keep the plan door first — it is the day’s tool, and its block is the one the practices re-evaluation ruled — and only the actions move. The foot row: Edit details · Cancel event · Delete as three equal 44px cells under a hairline, Delete in the danger ink and nowhere near the everyday tap; a mirrored tournament game shows its “only the organizer can…” sentence there instead, as today. Restyled the order at ≤640 · Unchanged the desktop drawer’s order (phone-only first, as the walk recommended; the desktop can follow later if you want one order), the deep links (?event=…&tab=attendance still selects a tab), the dialog’s Escape · Tab trap · focus return, the field floor on the list (A4), the mirrored-game and moved-game notes (they stay directly under the meta, where the sheet says where the game came from).

    Design intent — the floor. Every control on the sheet reaches 44px, and most of them by becoming what they already were on a phone: the tabs 35 → 44 (the underline row, taller); All in · Reset 27 → 44 beside the Attendance heading, the word “Season attendance” (a link to Insights, not a field control) moves to the foot of the list as a quiet row; the five count chips 24 → a 44px filter row, five equal cells, the counts at body size with the icon each chip already has; the twelve “Edit RSVP” buttons go — the whole 48px row is the tap, the status badge is its trail, a chevron says it opens, and the tap raises a bottom sheet from the foot of the screen: the player’s name, the event, the four choices as full-width 52px rows with the current one ticked, and the note field; tapping a choice saves it and closes the sheet (one tap per player after the row), a typed note is saved with the choice or when the sheet is dismissed (scrim, swipe, back). It is a sheet over the event sheet, so back and Escape close the inner one first, and focus returns to the row. The rows themselves share one white frame with hairlines, no gaps — the schedule’s treatment; the map link 21 → the where-line is the row (pin · venue · kit · chevron), the whole line opens the map; + Add final score 40 → 44, Edit score 36 → 44 as a pill on the scoreline, Add to the book 20 → a 44px quiet row, Give an award 35 → 44, Edit in Lineups 34 → 44 on the lineup tab. The Out ink goes one step darker — the baselined 4.41:1 at 12px is now 5.2:1 on the same tint (rgb 160 48 28 in the drawing; the build picks the token), and the badge word goes 12 → 14 because on attendance-taking the status is the looked-for value (A4: the field key at body). One deletion, flagged for you: the locked awards box before a game (“Enter a final score to unlock awards for this game”) is a sentence explaining an absence, on a game morning — by your own 4 September rule it does not render until the game has started; once a score exists the box is exactly as today. New the row-as-tap with its choices beneath, the where-row, the foot row · Restyled the tabs, the bulk buttons, the filter row, the score doors, the Out ink · Unchanged the words on every control, the RSVP choices and their icons, the note field, the autosave pill (transient, as ruled), the lineup and scouting tabs’ contents.

    A · More is a sheet

    1. On Overview, tap More. A sheet the full width of the phone rises from the bar, the page behind it dims, a small grab line sits at its top. No narrow popover on the right.
    2. The first row is Notifications with its count; then ONE Your teams list: UAT Test Team tinted with no chevron (you are here), and UAT Between Seasons on the same list with 2025 Season in small type at its right and a chevron — no second “No live season” header. (Changed on the walk, 20 Sep: the switcher had never been drawn; two headers over two rows cost 25px of the sheet.)
    3. Three tiles — Practice plans · Lineups · Skills & Goals. Tap each in turn; each opens its room in one tap and the sheet is gone.
    4. Below the tiles: Season (Tournaments) beside Progress (Insights); Money beside Communication (Email families); Team as four rows in two columns (Tryouts · Staff · Documents · Settings); Help · Sign out at the foot. Every label on one line — “Email families” included — and the side-by-side rows carry no chevron. Nothing scrolls inside the sheet on a 844-tall phone (a small scroll on a shorter one is fine). (Changed on the walk, 20 Sep: “Email families” wrapped at 390 and 360; the chevron on a half-width row was the 26px it needed — the word stays, the column gives.)
    5. Tap the dimmed page above the sheet — it closes. Tap More, then the ✕ in the bar — it closes. Every row is a comfortable tap; none feels short.

    B · One identity line

    1. Open Schedule. The bar at the top is ONE slim line — team name · record · the “?” — not the two-line block. The “?” is a whole disc inside the line, its top not sliced off by the screen edge. The page title sits right under it. (Changed on the walk, 20 Sep: the 44px tap circle was painted in full and its top 4px sat above the screen; the disc is now drawn 34px inside the same 44px target.)
    2. Scroll the list. The line keeps its shape — it does not shrink, grow, or lose the “?”. The “?” still opens the help drawer.
    3. Open Overview. It keeps the two-line masthead (club · season · record) and still collapses to the bare name when you scroll, as before.
    4. Open Chat and a room. No team masthead above the room: the room header alone, with the back arrow on the LEFT and the “?” on the right. Tap back — the room list.
    5. On the desktop (1200+): the masthead is unchanged — two lines, never collapses, the “?” at the right.

    C · “Saved” is transient revised 20 Sep

    1. Open today’s game from Lineups. At rest nothing says “Saved” anywhere — no word in the title row, no pill in the corner.
    2. Change one cell in the grid. A pill appears bottom-right, above the bar: “Unsaved changes” → “Saving…” → “✓ Saved” — then it fades out within about three seconds and nothing remains.
    3. Scroll deep into the grid and change a cell there. The pill appears in the same corner of the window — it follows the window, not the page.
    4. Change a cell, then another before the pill has faded. It comes straight back to “Unsaved changes” — no flicker, never a second pill.
    5. Open Practice plans → next practice → Open the plan. Edit the goal: the same pill, the same fade; nothing over the sheet’s foot at rest.
    6. Open Schedule → today’s game → Attendance. Change an RSVP: the pill in the window’s corner, then gone.
    7. Turn on airplane mode and change a cell. “Couldn’t save · Retry” appears and stays. Turn the network back on, tap Retry: “✓ Saved”, then it fades.
    8. On the desktop, the same: bottom-right of the window, fades after a save; the title row carries no word (one convention at every width).

    D · The field floor

    1. Open Game day (the Overview card or the Lineups room). Hold the phone at arm’s length: the position letters (RF · P · C · 1B) are clearly larger than before; “1 of 2 innings pitched”, “ON THE FIELD — INNING 1” and “BENCH — LONGEST SITTING FIRST” are readable without bringing the phone closer.
    2. “US — THEM” over the score is one line, and the inning stepper reads “INNING 1 OF 7”.
    3. Open next practice → Run practice. The “← PLAN · 3 BLOCKS” bar and the block rows read at the same comfortable size.
    4. The attendance list (C4): the count chips and “All in · Reset” read at the same size. Nothing outside these three surfaces changed size — the Overview tiles and the masthead’s meta line are still small (they are stage 1).

    E · Nothing else moved

    1. In More, tap UAT Between Seasons (no live season). Its More sheet shows Notifications, the teams, Help and Sign out — no tiles, no groups (a closed season is one page).
    2. Back on UAT Test Team: the demo tour, the “?” drawer and the notification badge on More all still work.
    3. Rotate to landscape or widen the window to a tablet (700–900px): the sheet is still full width; the masthead there is unchanged (two lines, collapses on scroll).

    0 · What this is

    What was measured (19 Sep 2026, dev, UAT head coach): 34 screens at 390×844, six at 360×780. Per screen: height in screens, words on the first screen, controls under the 44px tap floor, words at ≤11px, pinned chrome. Interactions driven: the More sheet, the Schedule’s three views and event sheet, a chat room, the live plan, the lineup grid, the console, the recording page, a roster row’s blank side. No sideways scroll at either width on any screen.

    PM brief

    Coaching from a phone

    docs/projects/active/COACH_MOBILE_EXPERIENCE_PM_BRIEF.md · 19 Sep 2026

    What we are proposing

    A staged re-shaping of the Premium Coaches Portal for phones — the way most coaches will actually use it in-season. Not a redesign: the screens, words, doors and data stay. What changes is the container each one sits in at phone width, so a coach with one thumb reaches the day’s tool in one tap and reads the day’s facts on the first screen.

    What a coach sees and does differently

    • More is a real sheet. Tap More and the whole menu rises from the bar — Practice plans, Lineups and Skills & Goals as the first three tiles — instead of a narrow list that scrolls inside itself.
    • One line says where you are. The team name and record sit in a slim line at the top of every screen; a chat room has one header, with back on the left. Stage 1 (ruled 21 Sep, built): a coach with more than one team switches by tapping the team name — a chevron opens a short sheet of their teams, and those rows left More; and every screen, the Overview included, wears the same one line, with the club and season in a quiet line under it on the Overview that scrolls with the page. Nothing jumps under the thumb, and the “?” never disappears.
    • The first screen fits the phone. Overview’s six tiles become six rows — the figure and one qualifier each, the whole row a door — and the game-day card’s two jobs become two full-width taps while its call time and kit join the facts line. Built 21 Sep: the Overview 948px against 1,104, all six rows above the bar at 390×844.
    • Schedule opens on today. The season so far folds above; week view skips empty days; month view shows dots and lists the day you tap; on game day the event opens on attendance and the lineup, not the score box.
    • Lineups start with the players. The setup controls fold into one line once a lineup exists; undo, redo, print and templates become one icon row.
    • Recording at practice is one tap per player. A player is a row; the dialog offers Next player; the tally and Review stay docked above the bar.
    • “Saved” stops sitting over the work. It appears only while something is saving and fades once it has; only a failed save stays, with its Retry.
    • The field is readable at arm’s length. The console’s positions and counts come up to body and support sizes.
    • Tables that fit stay tables. The attendance report is twelve rows, not twelve cards.

    Why it matters

    The portal was built desktop-first and adapted to the phone screen by screen; the adaptations are individually reasonable and cumulatively heavy — 131px pinned before content, a menu that hides half of itself, lists that open on April, a lineup whose first player is under the first screen. Coaches use this product at the fence. Every stage returns screen to the work and taps to the tool.

    Role-based differences

    None new. An assistant sees fewer doors in the sheet (the same gating as the sidebar); a viewer sees the read faces they see today. Nothing a coach cannot do today becomes possible, and nothing they can do today goes away.

    Trade-offs

    • Two layouts per screen where the phone diverges (rows vs tiles; folded vs open setup). Kept to the container, so copy and data have one source.
    • The bottom bar’s four tabs stay; the owner may swap Roster for a season tool after stage 2 if the sheet does not settle it.
    • Stage 5 (the player’s read face) waits for the roster and player page walk (§182).

    Priority and sequence

    Stage 0 first (the shell — cheap, and it lifts every other screen); then the first screen and the Schedule, which are the roads to everything; then game week, practice week, people, reports. Each stage is drawn on this hub, ruled by the owner, built, reviewed and walked before the next begins.

    Success criteria

    • Practice plans, Lineups and Skills & Goals each one tap from any screen.
    • Pinned chrome at rest ≤110px on every team screen but Overview; no screen with two stacked headers.
    • The Schedule’s first upcoming row on the first screen at 390.
    • The lineup grid’s first row on the first screen at 390 once a lineup exists.
    • No Saved pill at rest anywhere — it appears on an edit and fades after the save; no console text under 12px; the attendance report under 1,600px at 390.
    • The layout sweep green at 361/390/768/1440 on every touched screen, with the new field-floor rule.
